title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM)
authors: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel

pages.title: Generate by reversing a noising process

blocks.html: Forward process: start with a real image $x_0$ and add a small amount of Gaussian noise. Repeat $T$ times. After enough steps, the image is indistinguishable from pure noise.
Reverse process: start from pure noise $x_T \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$ and learn to gradually remove noise step by step, producing a sample $x_0$ that looks like real data.

DDPM shows that both the forward and reverse processes can be written as Markov chains of Gaussian transitions, that the reverse-process parameters reduce to predicting the noise that was added at each step, and that the resulting loss is a remarkably simple weighted denoising MSE.
We present high quality image samples using diffusion probabilistic models. ... a 256×256 sample matching the visual quality of GANs while remaining a likelihood-based model.

blocks.html: After $T$ steps you have $x_0$, your sample. The slow part: $T = 1000$ neural network forward passes per sample. Later work (DDIM, classifier-free guidance, Karras schedulers) cut this to 20-50 steps.

On CIFAR-10 unconditional generation, DDPM achieves FID 3.17 — at the time, the best result among likelihood-based models and competitive with state-of-the-art GANs (StyleGAN: 3.86, BigGAN: 14.7 on CIFAR-10 unconditional).
On LSUN bedrooms and CelebA-HQ at 256×256, DDPM produces samples that are visually comparable to GANs (sharp, coherent), without the mode-collapse failure modes.

DDPM made diffusion models competitive with GANs for the first time on quality, and they came with several big advantages: stable training (no minimax), strong likelihoods, easy conditioning, and natural multi-modality.

Direct descendants: improved DDPMs (cosine schedule, learned variance), classifier-free guidance, latent diffusion (Stable Diffusion), score-based models, consistency models, rectified flow. DDPM is the technical foundation of the image-generation explosion of 2022-2024 — DALL·E 2, Imagen, Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, Sora, Veo.
